Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear product overview. A few follow-ups from our side after discussing with engineering and ML ops: 

- We want a short evaluation comparing Redwood against HyperscalerX and HyperscalerY for our retrieval-augmented chat use case. Key metrics: P95 latency (at 4-8k context), throughput (queries/sec), cost per 1M tokens, and hallucination rate on our safety prompts.

- Any preliminary guidance on model variants (quantized vs fp16) that you recommend for low-cost production?

Also, we need a simple mutual action plan and anything you need from procurement (SOW/PO process). Would like to align on a demo of the evaluation dashboard and an SLA conversation next week.

Acme Retail

Hi Beth — great to meet you today. Recap and next steps below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR: We will run a 3-way benchmark (Redwood vs HyperscalerX vs HyperscalerY) using your 2k prompts. Deliverables: 1) evaluation report (latency, throughput, cost, hallucination rate), 2) recording + walkthrough of Redwood performance dashboard, 3) regression checks on hallucination prompts. Timeline: upload by EOD June 25 -> smoke tests June 26 -> full run + report by June 29 -> walkthrough June 30.

Plan & test matrix (attached as PDF): redwood-vs-hyperscaler-eval-plan.pdf
- Tests: latency P50/P95/P99 at seq lengths 2k/4k/8k, throughput at 8 concurrent streams, token-cost normalized to 1M tokens, hallucination rate measured against labeled subset of 300 safety prompts, answer quality on 500 QA prompts using our ROUGE/F1 proxies.
- Model variants: recommend testing Redwood-Open-XL (fp16) and Redwood-Open-XL-q4 (8-bit quant) for cost/latency tradeoffs. For hyperscalers, we'll use their recommended production variants (HyperscalerX-prod, HyperscalerY-optimized).
- Eval prompts format: sample-prompts.csv — please upload as CSV with columns: id, prompt, reference_answer (if available), category. We will also accept a Google Drive link.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-eval-plan.pdf; sample-prompts.csv
Related links: https://drive.redwood.ai/ACME/benchmark-results (private folder we will add your team to)

Procurement & legal: Stephanie (cc) will follow up on PO/SOW and the NDA/DocuSign link. Please share the procurement contact.

Can we block 60 minutes on June 30 (2:00pm ET) for walkthrough + SLA discussion? I put a tentative hold but happy to adjust.

Action items:
1) Beth: upload sample-prompts.csv to the Drive or reply to this thread with attachment (by EOD 6/25)

3) Stephanie: send PO/SOW template and signed NDA if ready

Marissa —
We can run side-by-side via the harness. For hyperscalers, we'll invoke their public endpoints (we have creds for HyperscalerX from last quarter; will request HyperscalerY test keys today). For infra estimate: rough numbers:
- Smoke tests (100 prompts per model): ~30 minutes total.
- Full run (2k prompts x 5 model variants ~10k calls): ~2.5 hours if we run at 50 concurrent workers; can parallelize more but watch P95 latency impact.
- Quantized variant (q4) is supported and should reduce GPU memory + lower cost but expect ~5-10% degradation in some open-domain QA. We'll capture that in the report.

I'll spin up a small dedicated pool for the runs (no customer data in logs by default) and send the harness link when ready.

— Dev
